summary: Pinned cohort resurrects to legacy variant after autoscaler preemptive restart during weighted canary
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteAble Labs observed a subset of requests from a pinned tenant suddenly returning responses from the legacy variant (redwood-13b-v1.0) while the tenant was enrolled in a weighted canary for redwood-13b-v1.2. This started during a burst of autoscaler preemptive restarts triggered by a GPU maintenance event.

Impact:
- ~3% of requests for tenant noteable-prod were served by legacy variant for a 30-minute window, causing mismatched output formatting and higher token usage.
- Customer reported 5 user-facing errors and quality regressions in their production traffic.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool node group: dp-us-east-1-group-a
- Orchestrator version: v2026.02.18+build-232
- Autoscaler: preemptive restart policy enabled; recent maintenance window 2026-03-10T02:00:00Z

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Weighted canary set to 5% v1.0 / 95% v1.2 for route /api/generate for tenant noteable-prod.
2. Autoscaler initiates preemptive restart on 6/42 nodes; prewarm jobs trigger while control-plane snapshots are being compacted.
3. For a subset of cohort cookies, subsequent requests were routed to legacy variant despite the tenant having a pinned cohort to v1.2.

Expected behavior:
- Pinned cohorts should retain affinity to the pinned variant throughout autoscaler restarts and prewarm, with fallbacks used only when explicitly allowed by policy.

Actual behavior:
- A reconciliation race allowed an older routing snapshot to be applied during node prewarm finalization, reintroducing legacy variant entries into the cohort mapping for certain session cookies.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- Edge logs: spike of 502->fallback routing events at 2026-03-10T02:03:12Z correlating with node restart IDs: node-42, node-37
- Orchestrator audit: snapshot_apply: snapshot_id=2026-03-10T02:02:59Z (stale), target_snapshot=2026-03-10T02:04:10Z
- Request tracing: trace IDs showing redirect to legacy variant include trace-ff12a, trace-ff17b

Immediate customer impact:
- Customer-facing errors and increased token counts. Finance notified for potential billing adjustment.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:21 - Maya Patel (Support): Customer reported unexpected model outputs and provided traces. Attached sample payloads and timestamps.

2026-03-10 09:05 - Jordan Alvarez (SRE): Acknowledged ticket. Beginning triage; coordinating with autoscaler team and control-plane owners. Temporary mitigation: enabled stricter prewarm snapshot gating for noteable-prod route.

2026-03-10 10:40 - Autoscaler Team: Confirmed preemptive restarts at 02:00Z. Found interplay with prewarm hook that marked prewarm finished before orchestrator snapshot apply completed on a subset of nodes.

2026-03-10 12:15 - CS (Maya Patel) to Customer: Notified customer of ongoing investigation and temporary mitigation (gating). Asked for confirmation if issue still observed. Customer reported intermittent residual errors for 10 minutes after mitigation.

2026-03-11 02:10 - Jordan Alvarez (SRE): Deployed hotfix to orchestrator snapshot reconciler to prefer latest snapshot by timestamp and to reject snapshot_apply if prewarm_finalize_time < snapshot.create_time. Patch rolled to us-east-1 pilot.

2026-03-12 17:30 - Customer (NoteAble Labs): Confirmed behavior resolved in production; no further legacy variant responses observed after 2026-03-11 02:20Z. Customer requested postmortem and billing review.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: snapshot race where prewarm finalization on preemptively restarted nodes allowed a stale snapshot to be applied. Evidence: orchestrator audit shows snapshot_apply of older snapshot id interleaved with prewarm completion events.

Findings:
- Prewarm hook reports finish before snapshot apply completed on ~6 nodes (node-37, node-42, node-44).
- Reconciler logic accepted snapshot if node reported prewarm_complete within a 5s window; race window widened during high restart churn.
- Pin mapping cache persisted on edge-proxy pods; edge cache invalidation TTL of 60s allowed stale cookie->variant mapping to be reused until explicit invalidation from control-plane.

Hypothesized root cause chain:
1) Autoscaler preemptive restarts created churn and short-lived prewarm events.
2) Orchestrator snapshot reconciliation accepted an older snapshot due to non-monotonic snapshot timestamps during compact/rotate.
3) Edge cache TTL and delayed invalidation caused some session cookies to re-resolve against the stale mapping, resurrecting legacy variant entries for pinned cohort.

Reproducibility: intermittent; reproduces under controlled high-churn autoscaler tests when snapshot compacting is enabled and prewarm gating is relaxed.
resolution:
Mitigations applied:
- Hotfix merged and rolled (PR #12345) to enforce monotonic snapshot acceptance and require prewarm_finalize_time >= snapshot.create_time before applying snapshot.
- Increased edge pin cache invalidation to 0s on canary routes during autoscaler maintenance windows and added explicit invalidation message after snapshot apply.
- Temporarily disabled preemptive restart policy for affected dedicated pool until full rollout.

Longer-term actions / follow-ups:
- Create an orchestration test that simulates prewarm + snapshot compacting churn (owner: orchestrator team; due 2026-03-20).
- Update runbook to include explicit pin-cache invalidation step in maintenance playbook (owner: SRE; due 2026-03-18).
- Billing adjustment requested by CS; finance to review token overage impact for NoteAble Labs between 2026-03-10T02:00Z and 2026-03-10T02:35Z.

Current status: Hotfix deployed to us-east-1; monitoring shows no recurrence. Customer validated resolution and requested formal postmortem.
